newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil whips to discuss re-election tactics.
newsitem.headline: Brazil whips to discuss re-election tactics.

text.p: Leaders of parties allied with the Brazilian government were due to meet on Wednesday to discuss a proposed constitutional amendment that would give President Fernando Henrique Cardoso the chance of a second term.

Dep. Jose Anibal, lower house leader of Cardoso's Social Democratic Party (PSDB), said the meeting would seek to resolve outstanding differences on the scope of the reform and establish some kind of timetable for its approval.

Anibal said he expected a lower house committee to begin discussing a version of the re-election amendment next week and that a first vote on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies might take place in December.
Constitutional amendments require two three-fifths majorities in each of Congress' two houses.
One question which the leaders would address related to whether or not sitting state governors and mayors taking office in January would qualify for re-election along with the president, Anibal said.

More than 20 of a total 81 senators are believed to be planning to stand as governors in the 1998 elections and some observers have said they might object to giving current state governors the chance to run again.
Anibal said the government intended to give current state governors and the incoming mayors the chance of a second term.

The deputy also said he expected the government would call an extraordinary session of Congress to run through at least of some of the Decemeber 15-February 15 recess to press ahead with re-election and other reforms.
